h1: Multi-specialty hospital software where every department reads the same record.
sub: HIMS runs a multi-specialty hospital as one system: a single patient record that cardiology, orthopaedics, medicine and surgery all write to, doctor rosters and queues by department, one pharmacy and one laboratory serving everyone, and a dashboard of OP, IP, beds and collections.

sections.h2: What multi-specialty hospital software has to do
paras: Multi-specialty hospital software has one job that a clinic system does not: keep many departments, each with its own doctors, queues and habits, writing to a single patient record and drawing on shared services. HIMS does this by treating a department as a view of the hospital rather than a separate system. Cardiology and orthopaedics see their own rosters and queues, but the pharmacy they prescribe to, the laboratory they order from and the bed board they admit to are the same for everyone.

For management the payoff is a live dashboard of the whole hospital: OP visits, admissions, bed occupancy and collections across departments on one screen, instead of a monthly compilation from each department's register. AuraPACS imaging is built in, so radiology is one more department on the same record rather than an external service.

sections.h2: A hospital with eight departments often has eight ways of keeping records.
sections.lead: Growth adds departments faster than it adds systems, so each one improvises.

items.p: A medicine patient referred to cardiology is registered again, and the first consultant's notes never reach the second.
Which consultant sits in which room on which afternoon is known to the department secretary and nobody else.

items.h: Every department wants its own pharmacy
items.p: Stock is split, expiry is missed and the same drug is reordered by three people.
Reports are printed in the laboratory and carried to the department, and a percentage of them arrive after the patient has left.
Department heads compile numbers for a review meeting, and the figures disagree with the accounts.

sections.h2: How a cross-department case runs on HIMS.

steps.p: UHID created at the first visit, reused at every department.
Token issued for the consultant on that department's roster.
The consultant refers to another department; the record goes with the patient.
Orders to the one laboratory, one pharmacy and AuraPACS, whoever raised them.
Bed allocated from the hospital board under the admitting department.
Charges from every department on the same bill; totals on the live dashboard.

items.q: Do departments get their own screens?
items.a: Each department has its own doctors, rosters and queues, and consultants see their own patients. The record underneath is shared, so a referral or an admission carries the full history. See doctor management software.

items.q: Does HIMS have specialty-specific EMR templates?
items.a: The EMR is structured for history, examination, orders, notes and reports and is used the same way by every department. Specialty-specific forms are not on record as separate modules; tell us what a department needs and it is scoped on the call.

items.q: Can the pharmacy and laboratory serve all departments?
items.a: Yes. There is one pharmacy with one dispensing queue and one laboratory with one worklist. Orders from any department land there and results return to the ordering consultant on the patient's record.

items.q: How is imaging handled across departments?
items.a: AuraPACS is built into HIMS. Any department can order a study, the study lands from the machine, the radiologist reports in the browser viewer and the report attaches to the record. See hospital PACS software.

The live dashboard shows OP, IP, beds and collections for the hospital, and doctor and department views show queues and load. How you want numbers cut for review meetings is set up during the project.

items.q: How long does a multi-department rollout take?
items.a: HIMS is delivered on a 30-working-day framework where scope allows. Larger hospitals usually go live department by department on the same record, starting with OP and billing. See HIMS vs hospital ERP if you are weighing a larger system.

items.p: The whole hospital on one platform.
